top_story: Trump escalated pressure on Iran at the UN with a threat to “annihilate” it if diplomacy fails, then hours later disclosed fresh US-Iran contacts, signaling a coercive negotiating track that mixes direct engagement with maximalist deterrence. That posture sharpens regional uncertainty as Yemen’s war intensifies along the Red Sea coast, where Houthi efforts to seize strategic high ground from Saudi-backed forces have killed up to 169 people in three days and displaced thousands. Gaza reflects the same wider pattern in civilian terms, with reconstruction constrained by ongoing bombardment and military control that turns recovery into an instrument of war governance rather than a path to stability. The regional picture is one of diplomacy operating inside escalating force, leaving civilian survival and political recovery subordinated to military leverage.
